bottom_line: Increased Red Sea security incidents are driving up shipping costs and causing route diversions, affecting oil, gas, and commodity flows.
what_changed: Frequency of security incidents along the Bab al-Mandab corridor has risen, with measurable disruption signals in port-flow and freight benchmarks.
why_it_matters: Operators routing through the Red Sea face higher insurance premiums and longer transit options around the Cape of Good Hope, with knock-on effects on commodity availability and lead times.
affected_actors: energy and bulk-commodity importers in Europe and Asia
main_uncertainty: Duration of the security escalation and the speed of any naval-coalition response.

scenarios.name: Sustained disruption
scenarios.description: Incidents persist, diversions become routine, premiums stay elevated.
indicators: premium indices remain above pre-crisis levels

scenarios.name: De-escalation
scenarios.description: Naval response and diplomatic channels reduce incident frequency.
indicators: incident count trends down for several weeks

watch_next: Insurance premium quotes for Red Sea transits
